summary: Enterprise evaluation for Dedicated capacity across NA/EU/APAC. Primary need: predictable throughput for global chat and rerank workloads, hard latency SLOs for end-user conversations, and multi-region reserved GPU planning with failover headroom. Strong security posture required (VPC + SOC2 + KMS). Procurement team engaged; legal + security review in parallel.
requirements: Workloads: interactive chat (512 token median), embeddings for search, model-based reranking for flight/pricing queries
Latency SLOs: p99 single-turn generation <= 150ms for 512 tokens (NA/EU), p99 <= 200ms APAC
Throughput targets: sustained 500 concurrent chat sessions global; peak burst planning to 1200 concurrent for marketing events
Availability: 99.9% regional SLA with cross-region failover within 60s
Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU region (hard requirement), logs retained per policy and accessible for audits
Security: SSO (SAML), enterprise KMS integration, audit logs surfaced to customer SIEM
Model policy: prefer open model variants validated for production; ability to pin model versions and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants on capacity pressure
capacity_plan: Requested reserved GPU pools (initial): NA: 40 A100-equivalent, EU: 20 A100-equivalent (W EU), APAC: 12 A100-equivalent (Singapore region)
Failover headroom: target 20% dedicated spare capacity per region for automatic failover (hot standby) + cross-region burst allowance of additional 10%
Burst policy: allow ephemeral burst across Dedicated pools up to 1.5x committed for 6 hours/day; billing delta to be negotiated
Sizing rationale: 40 GPUs NA covers sustained 500 concurrent chats with batching and KV caching; H100-equivalent conversion considered for 15% improved latency at 2x cost
Autoscaling: prefer predictable reserved + scheduled autoscale windows (Black Friday + promotions) rather than fully dynamic preemptible
sla_negotiation_points: Latency SLOs with objective vs. guaranteed tiers (p95 objective / p99 guaranteed) - customer pushing to include p99 in SLA, Redwood suggested p95 for contractual credit model
Uptime target: customer asks 99.95 for core inference endpoints, Redwood initial offer 99.9 with credits; legal wants cost/credit table
Failover windows: customer requests cross-region failover <30s; Redwood proposes <60s for cold/warm start, needs signed runbooks
Credits: request for token-cost protection during failover and capacity degradation scenarios
Penalties: capped credits not to exceed 50% monthly invoice; customer requests higher cap for enterprise critical flows
failover_strategy: Primary: regional Dedicated pool with hot prefix/KV cache replication where feasible
Secondary: warm pool in secondary region with KV warmup policies and early re-routing based on health probes
Tertiary: static model fallback (smaller quantized variant) to preserve latency under extreme capacity pressure
Network: private peering + multi-AZ placement inside region; require documented maintenance windows and pre-notification for planned capacity changes
